selected_controls.title: Disable SSH direct root login
selected_controls.threat_mapping: SSH lateral movement — root login via SSH allows immediate privilege escalation after credential theft; CRIMSON TIDE PHASE 3
selected_controls.verification_method: Verify PermitRootLogin is set to no in sshd_config and sshd -T output
selected_controls.justification: Root SSH login eliminates authentication barriers for attackers who obtain credentials; kill chain #1 (1x01) shows SSH as the lateral movement vector

selected_controls.title: Enforce SSH public key authentication, disable passwords
selected_controls.threat_mapping: Weak authentication — password-based SSH susceptible to brute force and credential stuffing; FINDING 009
selected_controls.verification_method: Confirm PasswordAuthentication no and PubkeyAuthentication yes in sshd -T output
selected_controls.justification: 1x02 vulnerability scan found SSH password auth enabled on all three servers; password attacks are the #1 initial access vector in healthcare breaches

selected_controls.title: Restrict SSH access to authorized groups via AllowGroups
selected_controls.threat_mapping: SSH lateral movement — unrestricted SSH allows any valid account to pivot between servers; FLAT NETWORK VECTOR
selected_controls.verification_method: Check AllowGroups directive in sshd_config; confirm only secops and admin groups listed
selected_controls.justification: Flat network topology (1x00) means any compromised user can SSH to any server; restricting to named groups shrinks the attack surface to admin-only

selected_controls.title: Configure SSH idle timeout and MaxAuthTries
selected_controls.threat_mapping: SSH lateral movement — unattended sessions and unlimited retries enable session hijacking and brute force
selected_controls.verification_method: Verify ClientAliveInterval 300, ClientAliveCountMax 0, MaxAuthTries 3 in sshd -T output
selected_controls.justification: Unattended SSH sessions were observed during 1x00 physical assessment; MaxAuthTries default of 6 doubles the brute-force window

selected_controls.title: Enable ASLR and restrict kernel pointer exposure
selected_controls.threat_mapping: Insufficient kernel hardening — disabled ASLR enables reliable exploit development for memory corruption bugs; LYNIS AUDIT
selected_controls.justification: 1x02 lynis audit flagged ASLR as partially configured; kernel pointers leak memory layout to attackers

selected_controls.title: Disable IPv4 forwarding and ICMP redirects
selected_controls.threat_mapping: SSH lateral movement — IP forwarding enables server-to-server pivoting; redirects enable ARP cache poisoning on flat network
selected_controls.justification: 1x00 network topology shows flat /24 segment; IP forwarding on servers extends the attack path beyond intended routes

selected_controls.title: Enable network sysctl hardening for SYN floods and martian logging
selected_controls.threat_mapping: Insufficient kernel hardening — SYN flood and spoofed traffic mitigation not enabled; MISCONFIGURATION ANALYSIS
selected_controls.justification: 1x02 misconfiguration analysis found default sysctl values on all servers; SYN cookies prevent resource exhaustion attacks on billing-srv-01

selected_controls.title: Enforce password complexity via pam_pwquality
selected_controls.threat_mapping: Weak authentication — default password policy allows trivial passwords; RISK REGISTER R-07
selected_controls.verification_method: Verify pam_pwquality module in common-password with minlen 14, dcredit -1, ucredit -1, ocredit -1, lcredit -1
selected_controls.justification: 1x03 risk register item R-07 identifies weak passwords as top authentication risk; healthcare sector sees 78% of breaches start with credential abuse

selected_controls.title: Set password aging and account lockout policy
selected_controls.threat_mapping: Weak authentication — no lockout allows unlimited brute force; no aging allows indefinite credential reuse
selected_controls.verification_method: Verify PASS_MAX_DAYS 90, PASS_MIN_DAYS 1 in login.defs; confirm pam_faillock configured in common-auth
selected_controls.justification: 1x02 scan found no lockout policy; 1x00 onboarding notes mention shared admin credentials that rotate never

selected_controls.title: Restrict database service exposure to localhost or private subnet
selected_controls.threat_mapping: Exposed database services — billing database listening on 0.0.0.0 exposes PHI to network traversal; SHADOW SYSTEMS
selected_controls.verification_method: Verify database service bound to 127.0.0.1 or 10.0.x.x; confirm UFW/iptables denies external access to port 3306/5432
selected_controls.justification: 1x02 network posture analysis shows MySQL listening on all interfaces on billing-srv-01; 1x00 shadow systems identified external DB connectivity as unmanaged

selected_controls.title: Disable unnecessary default services (avahi-daemon, cups, nfs)
selected_controls.threat_mapping: Unnecessary services — default daemons expand attack surface without serving business function; SERVICES.TXT
selected_controls.verification_method: Confirm systemctl status shows disabled/inactive for avahi-daemon, cups, rpcbind, nfs-kernel-server
selected_controls.justification: 1x02 services.txt lists 31 running services; 12 are non-essential; each unnecessary daemon is a CVE candidate

selected_controls.title: Audit and remediate SUID and SGID filesystem permissions
selected_controls.threat_mapping: Privilege escalation — unexpected SUID/SGID filesystem permissions provide root escalation paths; BASELINE SNAPSHOT
selected_controls.verification_method: Run find / -xdev -perm -4000 and -perm -2000; compare against CIS baseline whitelist; chmod u-s or remove unauthorized binaries
selected_controls.justification: Baseline snapshot (task 0) captured 23 SUID and 12 SGID binaries; CIS whitelist expects approximately 18 SUID and 10 SGID on Ubuntu 22.04. Filesystem permission review is critical for privilege escalation prevention

selected_controls.title: Install and configure auditd
selected_controls.threat_mapping: Missing audit visibility — no system call auditing means post-incident forensics cannot reconstruct attacker activity
selected_controls.verification_method: Verify auditd installed, enabled, and running; confirm /etc/audit/auditd.conf has disk_full_action and admin_space_left_action set
selected_controls.justification: 1x00 control inventory shows no auditing deployed; 1x01 kill chain analysis notes that lack of audit logs prevented detection of lateral movement

selected_controls.title: Configure audit rules for privileged commands and file access
selected_controls.threat_mapping: Missing audit visibility — privileged syscall auditing catches sudo abuse, crontab tampering, and passwd file modification
selected_controls.justification: 1x05 Crimson Tide advisory shows attackers modifying cron and passwd; without audit rules these actions leave no trace

selected_controls.title: Configure centralized log retention and rotation
selected_controls.threat_mapping: Missing audit visibility — short retention periods destroy forensic evidence; log-srv-01 must retain 365 days minimum
selected_controls.verification_method: Verify rsyslog forwarding from billing-srv-01 and web-srv-01 to log-srv-01; confirm logrotate maxage 365 on log-srv-01
selected_controls.justification: 1x03 security strategy specifies SIEM ingestion with 1-year retention; 1x02 found default 4-week retention insufficient for breach investigation timelines
